chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni said: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) that he said:

Know - may Allah teach you goodness - that Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, is Eternal. Eternity is an attribute that indicates to the wise that there is nothing before Him and nothing with Him in His perpetuity. It has become clear to us, with the acknowledgment of the common people along with the miracle of the attribute, that there is nothing before Allah and nothing with Allah in His permanence.

And the statement of whoever claimed that there was something before Him or something with Him is invalidated. This is because if there were something with Him, its permanence would not allow it to be His Creator, for it was with Him perpetually; so how could He be the Creator of that which was with Him perpetually? And if there were something before Him, that thing would be the first, not this one, and the first would be more worthy of being the Creator of the second.

Then He described Himself, the Blessed and Exalted, with names by which He called the creation when He created them, commanded them to worship Him, and tested them to call upon Him by them. He named Himself the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing, the All-Powerful, the Standing, the Manifest, the Hidden, the Subtle, the All-Aware, the Powerful, the Honorable, the All-Wise, and the All-Knowing, and similar names. When the exaggerators and deniers saw this from His names, and had heard us narrate about Allah that there is nothing like Him and no creature is like Him in His state, they said: 'Inform us, since you claim there is nothing like Allah and no similarity to Him, how do you share Him in the Beautiful Names and name yourselves with all of them? For in that is proof that you are like Him in all His states or in some of them, since you share the pure names.''

It was said to them: 'Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has assigned to the servants names from His own names with differing meanings. This is as when one name carries two different meanings. The proof for this is the common speech of people, which is permissible in their view, and which Allah used to address the creation and speak to them in what they understand, so that it would be a proof against them for what they neglected. A man may be called a dog, a donkey, a bull, a drunkard, 'Alqamah, or a lion, and all of these apply to him contrary to their literal meaning and his actual state. The names did not fall upon the meanings upon which they were built, because a man is not literally a lion or a dog. Understand this, may Allah have mercy on you.'

When we call Allah 'All-Knowing,' it is not with a newly acquired knowledge by which He knew things. He used His knowledge to preserve what is to come of His affairs and to exercise foresight in what He creates. By His knowledge, He knew what passed of what He destroyed; had that knowledge not been present with Him and aided Him, He would have been ignorant and weak. Just as we have seen that the scholars of creation are called knowledgeable only because of a newly acquired knowledge, for before that they were ignorant, and sometimes knowledge departs from them and they return to ignorance. Allah is called All-Knowing because He does not ignore anything. Thus, the Creator and the created share the name 'Knowledge,' but the meaning differs as you have seen.

And He named our Lord 'All-Hearing,' not with a part in Him by which He hears the sound and does not see with it, just as our part by which we hear is not capable of seeing with it. Rather, He informed us that no sounds are hidden from Him, not in the same measure as we are named. We have combined the name with 'Hearing' but the meaning differs. Similarly, 'Seeing' is not with a part by which He sees, just as we see with a part of ourselves that we do not use for other purposes. Allah is All-Seeing and does not ignore any person looked at. We have combined the name but the meaning differs.

He is Standing, not in the sense of upright posture and standing on a leg in the chest, as things stand. Rather, He informed us that He is Standing, indicating that He is the Guardian, like saying 'So-and-so is the man standing behind our affairs.' He is Standing over every soul for what it earned. 'Standing' in people's speech also means 'Remaining,' and 'Standing' also indicates 'Sufficiency,' as when you say to a man, 'Stand for the affair of so-and-so,' meaning 'Suffice him.' Our standing is on a leg; we have combined the name but not the meaning.

As for 'The Subtle,' it is not about smallness or brevity or littleness, but rather about penetrating into things and being elusive from being perceived. As when you say, 'This matter has become subtle for me,' or 'So-and-so is subtle in his manner and speech,' indicating that it is profound, dazzling the intellect, escaping pursuit, and becoming deep and subtle so that imagination cannot grasp it. Thus, Allah is Subtle, far from being perceived by a limit or defined by an attribute. Subtlety in us is smallness and littleness; we have combined the name but the meaning differs.

As for 'The All-Aware,' He is the One from whom nothing is hidden and nothing escapes. It is not through experience or reflection on things that experience and reflection provide knowledge, for without them he would not know, because whoever is like that is ignorant. Allah has always been All-Aware of what He creates. The 'All-Aware' among people is the one who asks to overcome the ignorance of the learner. We have combined the name but the meaning differs.

As for 'The Manifest,' it is not because He is above things by riding upon them, sitting on them, or climbing their peaks, but rather due to His subduing, overpowering, and having power over things, like a man saying, 'I prevailed over my enemies, and Allah made me prevail over my adversary,' indicating success and victory. Thus is Allah's manifestation over enemies. Another aspect is that He is Manifest to whom He wills, nothing is hidden from Him, and He is the Planner of all that He created. What manifestor is more manifest and clear than Allah? You do not lack His work wherever you turn, and in you are His signs that suffice you. Our manifestation is being apparent in oneself and known by one's limit; we have combined the name but not the meaning.

As for 'The Hidden,' it is not in the sense of penetrating into things by diving into them, but rather from Him is the penetrating of Him into things in knowledge, preservation, and planning, like the speaker saying 'I penetrated it,' meaning 'I knew it and learned its hidden secret.' Our hiddenness is being submerged in a thing and concealed by it; we have combined the name but the meaning differs.

As for 'The Subduer,' it is not in the sense of effort, exertion, scheming, dealing gently, or cunning, as servants subdue one another, for the subdued returns to be a subduer, and the subduer returns to be subdued. Rather, it is from Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, that all that He created is clothed with humility to its Doer, and its lack of resistance to what He wills is such that it does not escape Him for a blink of an eye, except that He says to it, 'Be,' and it is. Our subduing is as I mentioned and described; we have combined the name but the meaning differs.
And thus are all the names, although we did not name them all. Sufficiency for reflection is what we have presented to you. May Allah be our aid and your aid in our guidance and success.
ai.seo_question: How does Shia theology explain the difference between Allah's names and human names if they share the same words?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) elucidates the doctrine of *tashbih* (likeness) and *tanzih* (transcendence) by distinguishing between the linguistic sharing of divine names and their ontological reality, asserting that while humans possess contingent, acquired attributes, Allah’s attributes are essential and eternal. This treatise serves as a foundational Shia response to the Ghulat (extremists) and Mu'tazila, utilizing semantic analysis to prove that terms like 'Hearing' or 'Seeing' apply to God without physical organs or limitation, thereby preserving His absolute uniqueness (*fard*) against those who claimed similarity in essence.
